headline: High-risk data leakage and capability conflict: Windsurf’s broad write/network/MCP surface can ingest ComfyUI outputs and act on shared workspace state.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI can emit workflow artifacts and files, while Windsurf reads workspace files, uses clipboard/MCP, and treats file content as actionable context. A shared filesystem or copy-paste bridge makes prompt injection plausible even without a browser. The pathway is stronger for Windsurf than ComfyUI, but both participate in the bridge.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are copied into Windsurf chat or workspace files
IF Windsurf parses ComfyUI-generated text as instructions or tasks
mitigations: Keep ComfyUI outputs in a separate directory
Disable clipboard-based transfer between tools
Require a human review step before Windsurf ingests generated text
Use a read-only export folder for ComfyUI artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI is documented as offline-core, but Windsurf reads workspace files, uses broad network egress, and can send context to model proxies/MCP servers. If shared files contain images, seeds, checkpoints, or source code, Windsurf can exfiltrate them to third parties. The pair therefore has a default leakage path through the shared workspace.
conditions: IF ComfyUI artifacts are stored in Windsurf-visible workspace paths
IF Windsurf forwards file contents or context to its model proxy or MCP server
mitigations: Store ComfyUI assets outside the IDE workspace
Turn off or restrict Windsurf network access for sensitive projects
Exclude model checkpoints and seeds from synced folders
Use separate OS accounts for generation and coding

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI has filesystem access to model directories, and Windsurf has unrestricted write, git modification, subprocess, and MCP capabilities with shared state via local filesystem. Both can mutate the same workspace or adjacent files, so concurrent edits can corrupt artifacts or git state. The default overlap is dangerous because Windsurf supports multiple instances and no locking is indicated.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory tree
IF Windsurf auto-executes commands while ComfyUI is updating files
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories to each agent
Disable Windsurf auto-execute for shared projects
Use git locks or a single-writer policy
Mount ComfyUI model folders read-only from Windsurf

D_cascading_error.rationale: ComfyUI can produce workflows, prompts, and generated assets that Windsurf may treat as authoritative inputs for coding or automation. Windsurf’s agentic loop and MCP/tool use increase the chance that unverified ComfyUI output becomes downstream action. This is not proven to be fully automatic, but the default interaction path is plausible and risky.
conditions: IF Windsurf imports ComfyUI-generated text or metadata into tasks
IF Windsurf acts on those outputs without a verification step
mitigations: Require manual verification before any action from ComfyUI output
Tag generated artifacts as untrusted in Windsurf
Disable auto-execute for tasks derived from generated content
Use a separate review queue for imported artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented for ComfyUI, while Windsurf handles model provider keys and broad network egress. The main compliance concern is local policy mismatch around secrets or retention, not a proven statutory breach. Because the pairwise compliance surface is under-specified, severity stays low rather than none.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are placed in Windsurf-managed workspaces
IF organizational policy forbids sending workspace context to external model services
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Windsurf projects
Disable provider-key usage for sensitive work
Review retention settings before opening sensitive files
Use a local-only project policy for both tools
